summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease with multiple prior stents, hypertension, and dyslipidemia was admitted for evaluation of intermittent chest pressure and worsening fatigue. The chest pressure was atypical and not accompanied by other cardiac symptoms. Initial and repeat troponin levels were negative, and ECG showed no ischemic changes. A chest X-ray revealed no acute abnormalities. The patient reported that his symptoms of fatigue and dyspnea on exertion were consistent with his chronic mitochondrial disease, which often requires monthly IV hydration. Admission labs showed mild acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 1.6 mg/dL, which improved to 1.3 mg/dL with IV fluid rehydration. During the hospitalization, the patient experienced orthostatic hypotension and symptomatic sinus bradycardia, prompting a reduction in metoprolol dose and discontinuation of diltiazem. He remained stable, asymptomatic, and was discharged home with medication adjustments, including stopping diltiazem, reducing metoprolol, and switching from Nexium to ranitidine. Follow-up with cardiology was recommended.
